message.content:
Sure! Those numbers are already a pair of latitude/longitude coordinates – they point to the Googleplex in Mountain View, California.  
If you want to verify that with the Google Geocoding API (or just see the full address that the API would return), you can perform a **reverse‑geocoding** request:

```http
GET https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json
    ?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499
    &key=YOUR_API_KEY
```

### What you’ll get back

A JSON payload that looks something like this (truncated for brevity):

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "address_components": [
        {"long_name":"1600","short_name":"1600","types":["street_number"]},
        {"long_name":"Amphitheatre Parkway","short_name":"Amphitheatre Pkwy","types":["route"]},
        {"long_name":"Mountain View","short_name":"Mountain View","types":["locality","political"]},
        {"long_name":"Santa Clara County","short_name":"Santa Clara County","types":["administrative_area_level_2","political"]},
        {"long_name":"California","short_name":"CA","types":["administrative_area_level_1","political"]},
        {"long_name":"United States","short_name":"US","types":["country","political"]},
        {"long_name":"94043","short_name":"94043","types":["postal_code"]}
      ],
      "formatted_address": "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA",
      "geometry": {
        "location": {"lat":37.4224764,"lng":-122.0842499},
        "location_type":"ROOFTOP",
        "viewport": {...}
      },
      "place_id":"ChIJj61dQgK6j4AR4J7x5Z8YfXU",
      "types":["establishment"]
    }
  ],
  "status":"OK"
}
```

So the coordinates you supplied indeed resolve to:

> **1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA**

(That’s the Google headquarters.)

---

#### Quick sanity check

If you paste the coordinates into Google Maps or any mapping service, you’ll see the same address. The Geocoding API simply confirms that the latitude `37.4224764` and longitude `-122.0842499` map to the Googleplex.
